description.narrative:
CGIAR is a global agricultural network and the objective according to the organisation is to produce science for humanity's greatest challenges towards a world free of poverty, hunger and environmental degradation. The role of the CGIAR is to carry out research to support agricultural development as well as nutrition security and environmental sustainability. Previously known as the Consultative Group for International Agriculture Research, since 2010 it has been known simply as CGIAR and consisted of 15 Centres that carry out research in partnership with Universities, organisations belonging to National Agricultural Research and Extension Systems (NARES), the private sector and non-governmental organisations (NGOs), including farmer organisations. Since 2019 the organization has been undergoing a reform to "One CGIAR" based on the premise that CGIARs people, together with partners, can have more impact when brought together under fewer institutional boundaries and supported by empowered management, clear governance and an integrated operational structure. Currently 12 Centres have signed the Integrated Framework Agreement (IFA) that is the foundation of the new organization.
Sidas contribution to the CGIAR during 2019-2022 supported amongst others, the development and deployment of: crop varieties that are climate resilient, more resistant to heat, drought and flooding; crop varieties that are more nutritious, with elevated levels of essential micronutrients; agronomic practices that boost resilience and reduce the use of costly inputs; new livestock varieties, diagnostics, vaccines and medicines, to reduce the risks faced by pastoralists and livestock keepers (including antimicrobial resistance); evidence to support better policies that will help poor farmers use new technology to access markets, reduce risks and increase incomes. Research and Institutional capacity building will be advanced by partnering with national Agricultural Research and Extension Systems (NARES) and National Universities.
During 2022, Sida provided support to CGIAR through funding of Window 1 (pooled funding, undesignated). During the current phase (2019-2022) Sida has contributed in total 538 MSEK of wich 455 MSEK to Window 1 and 74 MSEK to designated pooled funding (Window 2). Funding under Window 2 came from Sidas strategy Hållbar miljö, hållbart klimat och hav, hållbart nyttjande av naturresurser 2018-2022 and went to Water, Land and Ecosystems CGIAR Research Programme (CRP) with MSEK 40, and to FISH CRP with MSEK 16.

CGIAR is a global partnership that unites organizations engaged in agricultural research, and its main activity is focused on increasing agricultural productivity in low-income countries. Sweden is considered to be one of the founders and has been supporting CGIAR since 1971. CGIAR will work specifically with: reducing poverty in rural areas, increasing food safety, improving nutrition and health and sustainable natural resource management. CGIAR contributes strongly to SDGs 1, 2, 3, 5, 6.13 and 15 and moderately to SDGs 8, 10, 12, 16 and 17. It is a priority task for CGIAR to develop knowledge and skills about biodiversity and how it changes in agricultural landscapes landscapes, forests and water systems. With new knowledge of biodiversity in agriculture, the scientific basis is built for a better understanding of the agricultural ecosystem and the best solutions to keep and protect biodiversity. In light of climate change, the need for new knowledge on biodiversity and ecosystems is increasing.
The research is conducted by 15 international centers that are members of the CGIAR System Organization in close collaboration with 3000 partners, including national and regional research institutes, civil society organizations, academia, development organizations and the private sector. CGIAR manages 11 biobanks to ensure the availability of processing materials for their own and their partners' use.
Sida decided 2017 to accept a new agreement structure for supporting the CGIAR Fund (at the World Bank) and CGIAR System Organization (at CGIAR System Management Office). The decision describes clearly the new CGIAR governance and management structure.
The support goes to the CGIAR Trust Fund, which is a Financial Intermediary Fund (FIF) with many donors including Sweden. The fund is managed by the World Bank and governed by a Funding Agreement with CGIAR System Organization. The funds are allocated in accordance to decisions made by the CGIAR System Council to 12 research programs and three research platforms after evaluation by an Independent Science Development Council (ISDC). The formal approval of the research programmes has been made by the System Council and Sida was represented at all meetings (a total of 19 meetings 2010-2019).
A total of SEK 506 million is proposed for CGIAR 2019-2022. One Appraisal of Contribution covering two strategies has been prepared: research cooperation and global cooperation on environment. It is proposed to support CGIAR during 2019-2022 with SEK 470 million as unrestricted support (Window 1) for CGIAR's research programmes (CRPs), platforms and CGIAR System Organization (Window 1), and SEK 36 million delegated from GLOBEN/INTEM to Window 2: of which SEK 16 million for the program on small-scale fishing (CRP FISH) and SEK 20 million for the Water, Land and Ecosystems CRP (WLE).
In 2018, Sida's support to CGIAR was SEK 115 million through Window 1 and SEK 8 million for the program on small-scale fishing (FISH CRP) through Window 2. The support suggested for 2019-2022 is somewhat larger per year. The previous phase covered 2013-2017 with SEK 664 million for Window 1. CGIAR's total budget for 2018 was USD 849 million and the three largest donors were the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, DFID and USAID with Sweden on seventh place. CGIAR's total budget 2019-2022 is estimated to be slightly larger per year than 2018.

CGIAR är ett globalt partnerskap som förenar organisationer som bedriver lantbruksforskning, och dess huvudsakliga verksamhet är inriktad på att öka produktiviteten inom lantbruket i låginkomstländer. Sverige räknas som en av grundarna och har stött CGIAR sedan 1971. CGIAR fokuserar på att minska fattigdomen på landsbygden, öka livsmedelssäkerheten och förbättra näring och hälsa och hållbar naturresursförvaltning.
Forskningen utförs av 15 internationella centra som är medlemmar i CGIAR System Organisation i nära samarbete med 3000 partners, inklusive nationella och regionala forskningsinstitut, organisationer i det civila samhället, akademin, utvecklingsorganisationer och den privata sektorn. CGIAR förvaltar 11 biobanker för att säkerställa att material till förädling för sitt eget och sina partners bruk är tillgängligt.
Sida beslutade 2017 om att acceptera en ny avtalskonstruktion för CGIAR fonden på Världsbanken och CGIAR System Organisation på CGIAR System Management Organisation. Beslutet belyser tydligt CGIARs förvaltningsstruktur.
Stödet går till CGIAR Trust Fund som är en förvaltningsfond (Financial Intermediary Fund, FIF) med många givare där Sverige ingår. Fonden förvaltas av Världsbanken och regleras genom ett s.k. Funding Agreement med CGIAR System Organisation. Medlen vidareförmedlas enligt beslut i styrelsen (CGIAR System Council) till 12 forskningsprogram och tre forskningsplattformar efter utvärdering av ett självständigt vetenskapligt utskott (Independent Science for development Council, ISDC). Det formella godkännandet av forskningsprogrammen har gjorts av det sk System Council och Sida har funnits representerat vid samtliga möten (sammanlagt 19 möten 2010-2019).
CGIAR informerade vid styrelsemöten i Addis Abeba och Chengdu i maj och november 2019 att forskningsprogrammen och plattformarna endast var resurssatta med mellan 80-85% av den godkända budgeten. Sida såg behovet av mer medel och hade medel så därför föreslås en genomsnittlig höjning och att ett större belopp utbetalas under 2019 då stora behov finns. Totalt föreslås stöd med 506 MSEK till CGIAR 2019-2022. Det görs en beredning men den täcker två strategier: forskningssamarbete och globala miljösamarbeten. Det föreslås stöd till CGIAR under 2019-2022 med 470 MSEK som stöd utan begränsningar (Fönster 1) till CGIARs forskningsprogram (CGIAR Research Programme, CRP), plattformar och CGIAR System Organisation (Fönster 1), och 36 MSEK som delegeras från GLOBEN/INTEM till Fönster 2: dels 16 MSEK till programmet om småskaligt fiske (CRP FISH) och dels 20 MSEK till programmet om naturresurser, Water, Land and Ecosystems (CRP WLE).
År 2018 finansierade Sida CGIAR med 115 MSEK genom Fönster 1 och 8 MSEK till programmet om småskaligt fiske genom Fönster 2. Stödet under 2019-2022 är något större. Den tidigare fasen omfattade 2013 till 2017 med 664 MSEK till fönster 1. CGIARs totala budget 2018 var 849 MUSD och de tre största givarna är Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, DFID och USAID och Sverige kommer på sjunde plats. CGIARs totala budget 2019-2022 uppskattas bli något större per år än 2018.

The CGIAR reports based on five impact areas.
1) Climate adaptation and mitigation
2) Environmental health and biodiversity
3) Nutrition, health and food security
4) Poverty reduction, livelihood, and jobs
5) Gender equality, youth, and social inclusion.
The results per impact area are reported upon through the CGIAR Dashboards. They present yearly results achieved by CGIARs Initiatives and Impact Area Platforms, providing access both to summarized results and to the detailed underlying data. The Dashboards draw on quality-assured information from the annual reports of the CGIAR Initiatives and Impact Area Platforms. At the moment, the yearly annual report 2023 and updated figures on Dashboard is available. The 2023 CGIAR Technical Report offers insights into how the CGIAR are forging ahead with new initiatives to deliver impact, and types of internal practices and reporting methods in place to improve and communicate its performance. Results are reported under four themes: 1) Genetic Innovation; 2) Systems Transformation; 3) Resilient Agrifood Systems; and 4) Regional Integrated Initiatives (cf. https://www.cgiar.org/portfolio-narrative/action-area-focus/).
Sidas contribution to the CGIAR during 2019-2022 supported amongst others, the development and deployment of: crop varieties that are climate resilient, more resistant to heat, drought and flooding; crop varieties that are more nutritious, with elevated levels of essential micronutrients; agronomic practices that boost resilience and reduce the use of costly inputs; new livestock varieties, diagnostics, vaccines and medicines, to reduce the risks faced by pastoralists and livestock keepers (including antimicrobial resistance); evidence to support better policies that will help poor farmers use new technology to access markets, reduce risks and increase incomes. Research and Institutional capacity building will be advanced by partnering with national Agricultural Research and Extension Systems (NARES) and National Universities.
The CGIAR System is a research network, but with a strong focus on partnership to bring research to impact and scale. The Makunda Makeover TV show in Zambia can be used a good and succefull example of this. The first reality TV show of its kind in Zambia, Munda Makeover, premiered on the Zambia National Broadcast Corporation (ZNBC) in November 2022. The farmer makeover show targeted smallholder farmers in Zambia to help scale out climate information services (CIS) and climate smart agriculture (CSA). Munda Makeover was facilitated by CGIAR initiatives and brought together the development, research, and commercial sectors to entertain and inform smallholders on CIS and CSA solutions and practices available to them, taking on the CGIAR Impact Areas of Climate Adaptation and Mitigation, and Nutrition, Health, and Food Security. The combined impacts of climate change, rising populations, scarce resources, and growing demand for food are undermining economic development and food security in Africa. The lack of access to technologies, such as smartphones and the internet, is a barrier to spreading knowledge and awareness among smallholder farmers. Life TV holds the potential to bridge this gap by engaging a wider audien The show focused on climate-smart agriculture and promoted best farming practices for crop, tree, and livestock production and marketing with departure from the needs of the farming family, with particular attention to womens role in farming. Agri-business SMEs were promoted in the show as essential actors in a thriving agricultural ecosystem. SMEs provide farmers with cost-effective and well-packaged technologies, as well as the necessary services, to improve farms and mobilize their farming potential. The objective was to increase farm productivity and profits while improving adaptation to climate change, with the overarching goal of delivering a climate-smart African future driven by science and innovation in agriculture. Munda Makeover travelled all over Zambia, connecting with farmers facing diverse issues, helping resolve them through expert advice and by interaction with other farmers. Each episode was 26 minutes long, composed of four- to five-minute features, introductions, and short promos. During each episode, the presenter and experts visit a family farm to demonstrate practical solutions that can be useful to improve farming practices and make useful changes on the farm, as viewers watch on The 20 episodes reached approximately 3 million people each week. It is now available, for free, on You Tube. The broadcast ran parallel to the main growing season, beginning with issues around soil testing, seed selection, and planting, then moving to pest and disease management, crop management, and all the way to harvesting, reducing post-harvest losses, storage, and markets. Issues around livestock management, financial inclusion, nutrition, and modern cooking solutions run throughout the entire season. To improve farmer knowledge exchange and learning, group approaches and cooperatives wew also featured.
Gender
There are two separate but interlinked issues regarding gender equality within CGIAR. The integration of gender equality and womens economic empowerment in CGIAR's research portfolio and research initiatives are essential priorities for Sweden The second issue is the integration of gender equality into the organisational structures of the CGIAR. Gender equality in the work place is important in itself and a necessity for the success of the research and innovations portfolio.
Each CGIAR Impact Area as defined in the 2030 Research and Innovation Strategy is supported by a dedicated Platform. CGIARs GENDER (Generating Evidence and New Directions for Equitable Results) Platform was launched in 2020. In support of CGIARs Strategy, this existing platform has transitioned into CGIARs Impact Platform on Gender Equality, Youth and Social Inclusion and is expanding its work to support the entire Impact Area. The Gender Platform:
Guides and amplifies CGIAR research, ensuring meaningful and lasting contributions to the global targets above. Strengthens the performance of gender and social science research within and beyond CGIAR by identifying the highest standards and setting strategic direction. Conducts independent research across the CGIAR portfolio, to synthesize evidence and fill gaps. Engages a wide range of partners, builds capacity and informs global policy discussions.
The recent evaluation of the Gender Platform showed good results and a promising way of working.
Regarding the organisational structure, the Gender, Diversity, and Inclusion (GDI) function was established as cross-functional support throughout the work of CGIAR. The main purpose is to provide expertise and guidance, tools and systems and to build consensus through advocacy. The GDI function is operationalized by a GDI framework and a GDI action plan.
The integration of gender in CGIAR is planned and structured with high ambitions. There are good policies and approaches enabling change, but a slow pace of achievement. Lack of mandate and expertise in the area of gender equality impedes the gender mainstreaming integration in CGIAR. There is a need for a development of the gender analysis in the organisation. Several indicators for the area are discussed but only partly complied with. The information is well-established thanks to the gender platform, the gender knowledge hub, the framework, the action plan, and the communication through HR in the organisation but needs to be better used.
Sida has for many years had gender equality as one of its priority dialogue points with CGIAR. As we mainly work through the System Council and the European donor group EIARD, we need to get them on board as well. Thanks to Sidas efforts, Gender in research and Gender in the work place are now standing items of the System Council agenda, maintaining it as a priority for the whole organisation. Furthermore, Sida has been instrumental in forming the group Friends of Gender with Australia, Canada, Germany and Sweden as core members. CGIAR is working increasingly strategically with gender issues, but there is still need for strong dialogue on the issue both regarding gender research in food systems, integrating in gender in food systems research, and gender in the work place.
Governance
The reform to OneCGIAR during 2019-2023 aimed at achieving a more comprehensive respons to global challenges through a more integrated and impactful CGIAR. The rationale behind being that today, research and innovation in food, land and water systems are crucial for a sustainable, climate-resilient world free from hunger and malnutrition and that new approaches, and a doubling of investment, are needed to ensure we can achieve the Sustainable Development Goals by 2030.
The reform considered both organisation and research programs. A new 2030 Research and Innovation Strategy was developed in 2020/21 with a mission to deliver science and innovation that advance the transformation of food, land, and water systems in a climate crisis. Later a new research portfolio for 2022-2024 was developed to operationalize the strategy. The big difference to previous portfolios was the multidisciplinary modus of programs that were shared by Centres, not focused on Centre thematics. There were platforms to lead the overarching work on prioritised areas such as the Gender and Social Inclusion Platform and Environment and Climate Platform. A wide range of stakeholders, including donors, were systematically consulted during the operationalisation.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
